name: Latin Liber Alchorismi
summary: A separate twelfth-century Latin textbook that expanded al-Khwarizmi-derived methods, covering whole numbers, fractions and square roots.
description: A separate Latin arithmetic exposition expanding and arranging al-Khwarizmi-derived calculation methods, including operations on integers and fractions and square-root extraction.
tier_reason: Retain the distinct expanded Latin reworking at fine detail; qualify the comparator for reordered chapters. This is a scoped consequence judgement, not a reward for documentation or representation.

date.label: 12th c.
date.basis: Folkerts groups the work among twelfth-century Latin adaptations; no exact composition year is established.

events.statement: A separate Latin arithmetic exposition expanding and arranging al-Khwarizmi-derived calculation methods, including operations on integers and fractions and square-root extraction.
events.caveats: The magister Iohannes named as author is not securely identified with John of Seville. The precise relation and order of Liber Alchorismi and Liber pulveris are not resolved here.

evidence.locator: Chapter 2, PDF pp. 18–19, paragraphs on LA and LA/LP
evidence.supports: Identifies this work as based on the arithmetic tradition and compares its operation sequence.

date.label: 13th-century manuscript
date.basis: Editors date the Oxford witness to the thirteenth century.

events.statement: The Oxford manuscript Selden supra 26 preserves an incomplete copy of the first part of Liber Alchorismi.
events.scope: Incomplete surviving copy of the Latin Liber Alchorismi arithmetic exposition; the presence of every integer, fraction and square-root procedure in the wider work is not verified in this witness.
events.caveats: The text’s adaptation is often dated to the twelfth century, but the surviving copy does not show the first actual readership; it is incomplete. The surviving witness supports access by its copyist; the copyist’s location and practical execution are not established. The Oxford witness is incomplete; the particular presence of every integer, fraction and square-root procedure was not verified.

links.statement: The Latin Liber Alchorismi expands the exposition of the al-Khwarizmi arithmetic tradition; Folkerts compares its chapter reordering with the Latin Liber Ysagogarum, not the lost Arabic original.
links.scope: Arabic arithmetic source tradition to a twelfth-century Latin exposition.
links.alternatives: Dixit Algorizmi, Liber Ysagogarum and Liber pulveris preserve other related redactions.
links.caveats: The lost Arabic original cannot establish a direct chapter-order comparison. Latin versions have distinct redaction and transmission histories.
links.timing: Both surviving Latin traditions have broad twelfth-century dates; the edge comes from the earlier Arabic-source node and does not impose an unsupported order on the Latin branches.

evidence.supports: Classifies LA among reworkings and compares its arrangement with the source tradition.
